node.comment: Took 350M when it was 378. Really fun class and not very stressful. I do think the projects could have been organized quite a bit better: people had no idea how well we were doing on the main project until grades came out. But they were all As. His lectures are a lot of fun, and honestly very useful in understanding systems/arch.
Professor Elnozahy has a strong curriculum and teaches effectively.

Mootaz is extremely knowledgeable and genuinely a really caring professor. The class covers a lot of content relatively quickly, so make sure to show up to lectures. Exams and programming projects are tough yet doable, but the TAs are super helpful, and you can argue for points back. Overall, a really good class. Be sure to ask Mootaz about Intel!
Mooootaz is the best :)

Professor Mootaz is a very caring and inspirational person while also being a great lecturer. Despite going into the class with skepticism towards the subject and the difficulty of the course, I grew to love both the content and the course due to his great lectures and non-trivial practice problems. Take a class with him if you can!

Professor Mootaz is the goat. His lectures are amazing for helping you understand the material and you will go pretty deep into the content and learn a lot. The class is pretty hard and there is a lot of work but there is opportunity for extra credit and your grade will probably be pretty decent as long as you put in the effort.

Professor Mootaz is awesome! His lecturing style is quite nice if you're used to it from OS, and I think the topics covered are vast. Grades wise, the exams require more reasoning than copying content from the lectures, while only being 15% each, so the class isn't too difficult to get an A in if that's your intent.
node.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

node.comment: Great professor, you can tell he cares about his students and the subject. Exams and projects are not graded leniently, and the content is VERY extensive and not particularly easy. Study a lot for the exams and write good code!

Dr. Mootaz is an amazing prof, you can tell he's got the experience by how knowledgeable he is. The lectures are masterpieces. The grading criteria kind of changed a lot over the semester (which felt off but I think he was mostly finding his groove). Exams were very tough, but lots of extra credit to make up for it. Projects live up to the hype.
Difficult class, but Professor Mootaz truly cares. Clear, approachable, and always willing to help. Makes learning manageable and enjoyable. Highly recommend.

Professor Mootaz is a great lecturer and actively does things for the well-being of students. Helpful and answers questions during office hours. Exams are not trivial and make up the majority of the grade, so study comprehensively.

Mootaz is probably one of the greatest lecturers I've taken. He is very funny, very knowledgeable about all things systems/computer science, and genuinely cares for all of his students. He cares that you learn the material first and foremost and has plenty of office hours to speak for that. If it's Mootaz vs ((any other os prof)), always pick him.
Nice professor, and cares about his students. Very helpful in clarifying misunderstandings or any questions you might have
My goat moo moo

Prof. Mootaz is a witty, captivating lecturer with a deep knowledge of CS & systems who truly cares about his students. He hosts 6+ OH hrs/week, replies quickly to emails, assigns no weekend HW, and loves entertaining students' questions. He grades holistically and offers ample extra credit. Mootaz has reignited my passion for CS; highly recommend.

Mootaz is the best professor I have had at UT. He is genuinely so caring about your well-being. He grades every thing very easily and even said we could write a paper at the end of the semester if we were going to fail to end with a passing grade. There is a quiz every day but it's just completion and the projects are okay but are graded easily

The absolute goat of OS, and is one of the most knowledgeable professors in the CS department. The class was chaotic due to it being his first semester teaching the course, and trying to copy Norman's system. Once he starts completely ignoring Norman's rules/syllabus I think he will be by far the best OS professor.

Great lecturer, but terrible time management. What drops his score are the changing/last minute announcements for EVERYTHING. We didn't receive any feedback for quiz problems (closest thing exams) until morning of test day, project grades released a month after expected date, dozens more such examples making the class unnecessarily more stressful.
Made OS easier to digest

Mootaz is a good teacher who clearly cares about his students. Assignments are very difficult and time consuming and exam and section problems were pretty difficult compared to in lecture content. Weird grading system punishes you for small mistakes, but there are many retake chances so its easy to pass if you put in effort but very hard for an A.

Dr. Mootaz is an amazing choice for OS. This semester, he was severely limited by the course structure he inherited from Norman, but I can see the class being more fruitful once he breaks free from Norman's stuff. I learned so much in this class and realized my interest in systems. The projects are tough but doable, and make sure your group is good

Mootaz is a great lecturer who explains hard OS concepts very well. He is approachable and willing to talk to students outside of class time. The course is difficult due to the rigorous projects, but the concepts made sense. The class was disorganized, but it was his first semester teaching OS, so he should get better in future semesters.

Great professor. I've learned a lot through his in-depth lectures. It's hard because it's OS.Very reasonable despite the various policy/syllabus changes. Class would be better organized once policies become clear and consistent.

In addition, he's very willing to talk to students outside of class and is always nice to his students. Would recommend!

It's OS. He's a good lecturer who clearly knows what he is talking about but seemed to be hindered by Norman's system. Grading parameters changed many, many times throughout the semester. Projects were very hard as well, requiring 30 hours a week (at minimum). Hardest and most time-consuming class I've taken but still happy I didn't take Norman!

Great lecturer. Obvious he has lots of industry and research experience. He isn't the most transparent about grading or general course policies, but it's his first semester teaching 439. It'll probably be better in the future. Projects are hard, so get an early start. Pay attention in lecture and never skip a day, even if it's not required.

He's a fine lecturer and quite funny in class, but the class organization was atrocious. Important information (like test and retake details) was often shared late, sometimes the night before at 10 PM. Also, (not moobonbon's fault), the grading scheme is just terrible, and the projects are difficult, making the class really stressful overall.

Very good professor and lecturer. Clearly has a lot of industry experience/knowledge. Explains concepts well and gives real-life applications. Grading system is still awful since it's Norman's and grading standards constantly changed throughout the semester. Most stressful class I've ever taken, expect to have many sleepless nights.

Overall, the class was really good. Mootaz is a great professor. He is open to any and all questions and answers them in depth, lectures were interesting and he throws in additional concepts and information.

Only complaint is it was very unorganized with grading. But generous with the retakes, you can get a good grade if you put in the effort,

The grading system is horrible, small mistakes in projects drop your grade by entire letters even if other grade categories are good. This is especially frustrating and demoralizing since so many darn people cheat on Pintos, which is a genuinely hard project. Nothing against Mootaz though, the class is just broken as it promotes a lot of cheating.

Mootaz is a pretty funny guy and had really enjoyable and interesting lectures. The one thing I think held back the class a lot was trying to incorporate aspects of Norman's syllabus (the grading scheme especially). Also, the class felt VERY disorganized and hectic at times as there were constant changes to grading policy and the class in general.

He's one of the best CS professors! His lectures are informative, and I felt like I truly learned, unlike in other CS classes. However, I hated the grading system (from Norman's). Grades are unclear unless you calculate them yourself, which is hard since some grades aren't released on time. It is a very difficult class but his lectures make it good

He's clearly a nerd about OS/Computer Systems, and his lectures are great. Him and Norman clearly had complications in organizing the syllabus this semester, but hopefully they worked it out for the future. The class is extremely hard, but that's what makes that UTCS degree worth it right? Treats you like a responsible adult unlike Norman lol.

The start was very cool, comp arch / OS with focus on energy. Kinda then turned into him explaining random stuff (super computing, cloud computing, blockchain), and then adding on stuff about energy consumption in these settings. It was kinda interesting, but whole course wasn't as low-level as expected. The hwmk and proj was jank, but lax grading.

I wrote the first review. Things were constantly changing throughout the semester and tests were rough, but they weighed the least out of all of the criteria. The prof really did take this to mind, as he's offering it for the first time,  and was actually very generous with the grading. Interesting lecturer and material if into 429 stuff

Dr. Elnozahy presented intriguing and important topics. The class is writing and research heavy, but I enjoyed the in-depth exploration. Grading and project criteria changed with short notice, but I'm sure that will be ironed out in the future. Tests can be tricky but I felt the course was graded generously overall.

Had to write a small paper every week and a final paper, yet no writing flag was advertised for the class. Final project was completely changed in multiple places within 48 hours of the deadline, yet there was very little grace to accommodate this. Homework grading is harsh and tests have few questions and are critically graded. Funny professor tho

Many last minute changes through the semester. It's a little understandable since it's the first semester for the course, but it shouldn't be at the expense of our grades especially considering the lack of any curves. Barely responds on Ed. It seemed that we were expected to have a solid background on CS439 (OS) and CS429 (CompArch) as well.
based

It's clear the professor is extremely knowledgable in the field, but course objectives & criteria were constantly changing. Many things were not announced till last minute, w/o further explanation. It's the 1st sem this is being offered, so mb these things will be improved on, but I found the course hard to follow along with due to these issues.
